messages:
alex: starting staged rollout v2026.3 -> 5% eu-central + eu-west (canary). No schema changes. deploy-bot kicked it off. Please watch latency/5xx/kv misses and call stop if anything fishy.

deploy-bot: [DeployBot] rollout id r-331b started: v2026.3 -> 5% eu-central, eu-west (profile: balanced). Monitors: latency, 5xx-rate, kvcache.

maria: quick heads-up, embedding p95 in eu-central jumped from ~380ms to ~720ms in small sample. Not many 5xxs yet but tail is rough.

sam: can you share request ids and whether the canary nodes are warmed?

maria: sample ids: req/5531, req/5532. Nodes: eu-central warm 2/3, eu-west warm 4/4. Logs:
```
kv_prefetch_hit: 28% -> 16%
latency_tail_spike @ 2026-03-23T16:12:04Z
```

jia: is there an auto-fallback policy for the canary route?

ops-lead: policy will auto-pin to stable v2026.2 if p95 > 1.6x baseline OR if 5xx uplift > 0.4%. Current p95 uplift eu-central ~1.89x. Trigger is met for eu-central.

alex: suggests soft-stop: PAUSE eu-central and route traffic back to v2026.2 (pin), leave eu-west running. That lets us investigate infra warming/kv misses without aborting whole rollout. Thoughts?

sam: +1 soft-stop eu-central. Prefer not to hot-rollback entire region.

infra-oncall: I'll spin two extra warm instances in eu-central and enable kv-prefetch flag on the canary route. ETA 6 minutes.

deploy-bot: [DeployBot] pausing r-331b for eu-central. To pin: `rbctl pin r-331b eu-central v2026.2 --reason "p95 embed regression"`

maria: pin applied successfully. Starting a small eval comparing outputs v2026.3 vs v2026.2 on the anomaly set.

jia: nice. After infra warms, we should re-run a 1% quick probe (not 5%) to validate tail behavior before resuming 5%. Also add stricter guardrail: if p95 > 1.3x in probe -> auto-abort.

ops-lead: agreed. Plan recap:
- pin eu-central -> v2026.2 (done)
- infra: warm + kv-prefetch (infra-oncall)
- maria: run eval diff and post results
- run 1% probe in eu-central for 10 minutes with tightened guardrails
- if probe looks good, resume 5% with gradual 1% increments and monitoring

alex: I'll add a short note to release notes and flag this in the changelog. Also will create a follow-up to investigate what caused kv-prefetch benefit to drop.

infra-oncall: warmup complete and kv-prefetch enabled. Observability shows kv hit rate climbing back toward baseline.

maria: eval diff shows output equivalence within tolerance for our test prompts. Latency p95 trending down to ~1.05x baseline during warm window.

sam: ready to run 1% probe?

deploy-bot: [DeployBot] launching probe: r-331b eu-central -> 1% for 10m (guardrail: p95 <= 1.3x, 5xx <= 0.2%).

ops-lead: monitoring. If any alert, call immediate abort.

(deploy-bot) 10m later: probe complete, metrics within guardrails.

jia: given probe success, thumbs up to incrementally raise to 5% after 10m stabilization. We'll keep stricter thresholds for next 30m.

alex: resuming 5% in eu-central now. document: rollback plan intact, pin available if needed.

deploy-bot: [DeployBot] r-331b eu-central resumed -> 5% (complete).

maria: monitoring — p95 stable, kv hit recovered. Leaving open for postmortem and infra action item to ensure kv-prefetch defaults for similar routes.

sam: thanks all. tagging @oncall for visibility :rotating_light:

ops-lead: marking action items: (1) ensure kv-prefetch auto-enabled for canary routes with heavy embedding tails, (2) add probe step to staged rollout checklist, (3) postmortem in next retro. Closing thread once items tracked.
